question: Can a bounded increase in fore/aft reference range complete measured support transfer and the full recovery-to-walking task while preserving joint feasibility, contact release requirements, motor caps and existing time budgets?

native_component.selection: Only the distinct V52 policy selects the new bias bound. Validate memory, support-transfer clamping and coordinate recentering against that same explicit bound. The scalar controls a body reference; actual hip and knee limits and actuator caps are unchanged.
native_component.compatibility: All predecessor policy and memory identities retain the 0.25 bound and original bytes. Never inject extended-range memory into V51 or change its profile digest.
native_component.retained_laws: Preserve V51 all-leg IK and reach reserve, 20 mm height-correction range and its rate bound, foot anchoring and paths, support contact predicates, startup law, reference/motor slew, feedback, energy accounting and no-cheat checks.
native_component.receipt: Expose the selected reference bound in the V52-specific evidence without adding fields to predecessor outputs.

geometric_basis.scope: Frozen terminal pose and fixed foot targets only; not predicted physical response.
geometric_basis.rejected_minus_035: No joint-feasible height on the original 20 mm grid for these terminal targets.

production_route.scope: A distinct successor of the complete R10K route. Preserve its ramp/hold and separate partial/prone recovery histories, then use a fresh V52 session for finite walking and stopping.
required_surfaces: exact DLL and native policy registration
immutable candidate, schedule, start, entry, route and finite-task contracts
real sampler, facade, worker and motor application
launcher seed and role declaration and source binding
complete native report and negative controls for preparation, partial recovery, prone recovery and walking
production_route.unchanged_task: Preserve all R10K entry, recovery, finite walking, four-cycle, 120-command stop, settled tail, whole-envelope and solver/time requirements. Only native walking reference range and successor identities change.

additional_branch_diagnostic.label: R10L-DEVELOPMENT-PREFIX-243-SINGLE-KICK-V1
additional_branch_diagnostic.prerequisite: The exact selected R10L pair must close valid and positive under independent audit.

development_coverage.adequacy: The phase-241 pair covers the exposed no-kick transfer refusal and partial-fall branch. The separate phase-243 kicked diagnostic covers the mutually exclusive genuine-prone branch. Both are development on exposed phases; neither is held-out evidence.
development_coverage.reuse: Fresh attempt and child identities, fresh world/setup and baseline. Never continue the old child, reuse its baseline, or run the unopened peer under the consumed R10K attempt.

required_validation: Native memory, clamp and recenter boundaries at 0.30 for V52 and unchanged 0.25 for predecessor policies; reject nonfinite and crossed-policy states.
Reproduce original V51 native responses including its command-840 refusal with the new DLL.

Use declared copies of pre-timeout exposed requests to demonstrate the new bounded reference and joint-feasible height through actual native APIs; do not reset preparation clocks or fabricate readiness.
The original 240-command deadline must still refuse an unready request under V52. Retained measurements do not become a new physical trajectory.
Verify stateless and session output agreement, complete native memory evolution, actual adapter/motor application and cold report replay before fresh physics.
Run the complete applicable source-bound safety gate on the assembled production route before fresh development.
After successful development, declare and qualify a new held-out finite decision, independently close its result and adopt successful evidence into QSDK-R10/M07.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: The reference was saturated for 67 commands and the final body was settled below the release margin. More time does not supply additional reference range.

alternatives.choice: Lower the required support margin or omit the remaining foot cycle
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Does not satisfy the intended existing finite walking and measured-support requirements.
The frozen terminal targets have no feasible pose within the existing height correction and joint constraints at this bound.

alternatives.choice: Select 0.30 with existing native feasibility guards
alternatives.advantage: Provides bounded range beyond the 0.28 terminal geometric target while preserving all task thresholds.
alternatives.risk: Changed geometry can change contacts, transfer timing and later walking. Only fresh physics can establish success; other phases may still fail.
